Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

promise verb

also make a promise, I promise, promise to come

classical

Plin. Ep. 1.15.1: prōmittis ad cēnam, nec venīs?
Traupman 365: prōmittō, promise

prōmittō, prōmittere, prōmīsī, prōmissum

verb, third conjugation

With an accusative, or a future infinitive: prōmittō mē ventūrum esse, I promise I’ll come. Prōmittere ad cēnam, to promise to come to dinner (Lewis & Short). The noun, a promise, is prōmissum; one’s word, fidēs (see word, promise).

Other words

  • polliceor, pollicērī, pollicitus sum — promise, offer

    verb, second conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 7.5.1: quam eram solitus dē meā pollicērī; Traupman 106: nihil certī polliceor, I’m not making any definite promise

    Lewis & Short: “to hold forth, offer, promise”; often of what one offers to do for someone.

  • spondeō, spondēre, spopondī, spōnsum — promise solemnly, pledge; vouch for

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Plaut. Capt. 898c–898d: Spondēn' tū istud? — Spondeō.; Cic. Phil. 5.51 (Lewis & Short): prōmittō, recipiō, spondeō

    The word of the Roman contract made by question and answer, spondēsne? spondeō (Lewis & Short); also of promising a daughter in marriage.

Examples

  • heus tū! prōmittis ad cēnam, nec venīs?

    Hey, you! You promise to come to dinner, and then you don’t turn up?Plin. Ep. 1.15.1

  • plūs ego polliceor: nīl recitābō tibi

    I promise you more: I won’t read you a thingMart. 11.52.16

  • Spondēn' tū istud? — Spondeō.

    Do you promise that? — I promise.Plaut. Capt. 898c–898d

See also word, propose.
